content:
olivia: Quick heads-up — vendor 'AndesAnalytics S.A.' submitted invoice for $37,500 and says the Chilean payer rules require a 5% withholding on services. They asked if Redwood can gross-up so they receive the full amount. Invoice PDF: https://files.example.com/andes-37400.pdf
raja: Do we have the vendor's tax residence on record? need RUT/CUIT and whether they claim any treaty benefit. Without TRC we should assume domestic withholding applies.
olivia: They gave RUT 76.123.456-7 in the invoice metadata. Said they are a Chilean S.A. No TRC attached.
ana: quick q — is this classified under our vendor master as 'services' (taxable) vs 'software license' (might be treated differently)?
benji: Product side — vendor says work was consulting for infra config. It's services. No software license.
raja: OK — for Chile cross-border services, withholding is typical. If vendor requests gross-up, we need: (1) signed request and justification, (2) copy of their tax ID (RUT) and vendor registration, (3) proof of tax residency (TRC) if claiming treaty (Chile — US treaty may not eliminate withholding for services). Also need contract allowance for gross-up.
olivia: Filing the docs we have to the thread: invoice + vendor onboarding snapshot. Link: https://files.example.com/vendor-andes-profile.pdf
ana: Contract says vendor bears tax unless we agree in writing to gross-up. So we need an approval and budget to cover the extra.
benji: How much would gross-up be roughly? quick calc pls.
olivia: Paste calc below:
```
invoice_amount = 37500
withholding_pct = 0.05
net_to_vendor = invoice_amount * (1 - withholding_pct)  # 35625
gross_up_needed = invoice_amount * withholding_pct / (1 - withholding_pct)  # ~1875
# so we'd pay ~37500 + 1875 = 39375 to cover the 5% withholding so vendor nets 37500
```
raja: Math looks right. Note: gross-up increases our invoice liability by ~5%. Also VAT implications? Chile invoice may include IVA — vendor's invoice doesn’t show IVA line, flagged as services (exempt/locally withheld). We'll confirm with vendor.
tax-bot: Automated reminder: gross-up requests > $10,000 require tax team review + CFO sign-off per policy. Attach TRC or equivalent per-country residency evidence before payment.
matt: I'm in. I can approve gross-up if tax confirms docs and procurement updates PO. Olivia — prepare approval email and updated PO numbers, route to me for signature. :+1:
olivia: Thanks — I'll collect TRC or official residency doc and request signed gross-up addendum from vendor. If we can't get TRC, do we proceed with net payment and remit withholding?
raja: If no TRC, we must withhold and remit per Chile rules. But get vendor to sign waiver or accept net payment. If vendor insists on gross-up and can't provide TRC, CFO approval still required and we should hold extra withholding in tax suspense account until clarified.
ana: Ops note — accounting needs clear GL code for gross-up expense and withholding tax payable. We'll also need to update AP instruction: pay 39375 to vendor bank after gross-up approval, and file withholding remittance with Chilean tax office for the withheld portion.
benji: timeline — vendor asked for payment within 10 business days. Can tax/legal expedite TRC check?
raja: I'll ping our local Chile consultant to verify TRC format and estimated turnaround. If they cannot deliver TRC within 3 business days, recommend we pay net and remit withholding to avoid late payment penalties.
olivia: I'll ping vendor for TRC and signed addendum now and post updates here. Thanks everyone. :slightly_smiling_face:
matt: Approved contingent on receiving TRC or explicit vendor acceptance of net payment. Keep me copied in approval email.
olivia: noted — will update thread when vendor responds.
